fixes.explanation: Close, baker, but this one is flipped. Moses tells Israel the LORD said to him, “You shall not cross the Jordan.” So he isn't the one leading them over. The LORD Himself goes across ahead of the people, and Joshua goes across ahead of them too.

Yes, baker. The LORD has Moses write the song down and teach it to the Israelites so it stands as a witness for Him against them. Then He says it “…will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.” So this song is meant to be sung, and sung for a long time.

Nice thought, friend, but the song isn't a party playlist. The LORD has Moses write it down and teach it to the Israelites so it stands as a witness for Him against them. That makes it more like a smoke detector than a victory song. Crossing the Jordan isn't its job.

Right, baker. Moses gave the law to “…the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.” That's two groups, not one keeper. I think that's smart, because I wouldn't trust my recipe to just one person either, and my hands are a mustache.

That's it, baker. Moses says, “Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officers…” He wants them in front of him so he can speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them. So the room he asks for is Israel's own leaders, tribe by tribe. These are heavy words, and he wants those leaders there to hear them.
